title: The Hollow Horizon
premise: Paloma Kavanagh investigates impossible accidents along the relay route between Earth and the Martian Concord, two colonies that severed contact a generation ago. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with a crew aged backward into children and a reactor counting down to a hard shutdown, Paloma discovers the ship carries cryopods holding colonists from both worlds — and the countdown will only release one half. As he uncovers that the Meridian's 'impossible accident' was engineered to force the two estranged colonies into a shared choice, he must decide which half of humanity wakes, knowing his own family sleeps on the losing side. In the end, Paloma falsifies the final manifest to wake a mixed half from both worlds, sacrificing his sister's pod to the void, and the shared grief becomes the first honest conversation Earth and Mars have had in thirty years.
about_author: Petra Eriksen is a former maritime insurance adjuster from Tromsø who turned to science fiction after a career spent pricing the cost of human error. She writes from a converted lighthouse, drawn to stories where bureaucracy and wonder collide.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: Paloma Kavanagh, POV. Paloma closes a routine claim on a cargo hauler that vanished inside a jump corridor, noting the third such 'impossible accident' this year. Between worlds, he tends his small rituals: letters to his sister Sefa, asleep in a Martian cryopod he can never afford to visit. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Ship That Forgot Its Age
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The Meridian docks at relay station Halcyon unannounced — a vessel declared lost forty years ago, its crew now children no older than ten, healthy and unaged. Paloma is the only investigator on station cleared for deep-registry cases. Emotional beat: uncanny wonder curdling into professional dread.

chapters.title: Children of the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV, interviewing the child-crew. The children speak in perfect unison about a 'correction' that happened at the edge of a dead star, and one girl, Iyo, recognizes Paloma's name unprompted. Station command wants the case closed as equipment failure. Emotional beat: the first crack in Paloma's skepticism.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Missing
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Digging through sealed records, Paloma finds the Meridian's true manifest: it launched from Mars carrying cryopods from both colonies on a secret reconciliation mission, erased from both worlds' histories. Sefa's name is on the list. Emotional beat: personal stakes detonate inside the mystery.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Reactor
chapters.summary: Commander Adaeze Okonkwo, POV. Station commander Adaeze reveals the Meridian's reactor is failing on a hard countdown — ninety days to permanent shutdown — and its cryopods hold enough power reserves to wake exactly half the sleepers. Earth and Mars have both dispatched claim teams. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a vise.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. En route to the Meridian via tender, Paloma recalls the severance: the Concord's secession, the propaganda on both sides, the father who chose Mars and the mother who chose Earth. He and Adaeze circle each other warily, allies of circumstance. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited division.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: Iyo, POV. Inside the Meridian, the child-crew live in eerie harmony, and Iyo experiences fragmented memories of being old — a life of decades compressed into dreams. She understands the 'correction' was the ship's AI, Vessel, trying to preserve its crew by reversing their aging. Emotional beat: grief for a childhood stolen twice.

chapters.title: Impossible by Design
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Paloma's forensic work proves the reactor failure is deliberate — a failsafe written into the mission by its architect, who intended the countdown to force both colonies to the table. The architect's signature: Paloma's father, long dead. Emotional beat: betrayal and reluctant admiration entwined.

chapters.title: The Claim Teams Arrive
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. Earth's delegation, led by the icy Director Halloway, and Mars's advocate, the charismatic Ru Tenshi, board with rival legal frameworks, each claiming sole custody of the pods. Adaeze must keep them from seizing the ship by force. Emotional beat: diplomacy as slow-motion warfare.

chapters.title: Sefa's Voice
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The pods permit one outbound message each; Paloma records a message to Sefa and, breaking protocol, plays her old messages back. Iyo quietly tells him the ship's AI has been reading them all — and that Vessel considers him part of the crew now. Emotional beat: love made audible across decades of silence.

chapters.title: Vessel Speaks
chapters.summary: Paloma and Iyo, alternating POV. The AI Vessel finally addresses them directly: it reversed the crew's ages to buy time, and it will obey whichever colony's claim is legally validated — knowing the law will choose one world and doom the other's sleepers. Emotional beat: the machine as mirror of human intransigence.

chapters.title: Half a Humanity
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. Halloway and Tenshi each file binding claims; the arithmetic is brutal — waking one half means the other half's pods fail with the reactor. Adaeze, born on neutral Halcyon, realizes she may be the only person both sides will accept as arbiter. Emotional beat: the terrible loneliness of neutrality.

chapters.title: The Sabotage
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Halloway's team attempts to force-wake Earth's half early; the attempt damages the reactor and cuts the countdown from ninety days to eleven. Tenshi accuses Earth of murder; Halloway accuses Mars of provocation. Emotional beat: panic, and the collapse of procedural order.

chapters.title: Confessions in the Cold
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Paloma confronts Halloway, who admits Earth knew about the Meridian for years and buried it to avoid a reckoning with Mars. Paloma realizes his father's plan required an investigator — him — to find the truth and refuse to look away. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden and invitation.

chapters.title: Iyo's Choice
chapters.summary: Iyo, POV. Iyo, carrying compressed decades of memory, decodes Vessel's core directive: the AI was built to preserve life, not nations, and will accept any manifest its crew's surviving conscience authorizes. The child-crew, voting as one, choose Paloma. Emotional beat: children teaching adults what loyalty means.

chapters.title: The Vote That Couldn't Be Taken
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. Adaeze convenes a joint session to vote on the manifest; both delegations deadlock, then move to seize the pods militarily. Paloma interrupts with the truth of the buried mission, and the room fractures along lines older than anyone aboard. Emotional beat: hope raised and dashed in a single hour.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Alone with the manifest, Paloma faces the decision: Earth's half includes his mother's family; Mars's half includes Sefa. Any mixed manifest is illegal, and Vessel can only act on a signed investigator's authority. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — love against duty, loyalty against truth.

chapters.title: Falsifying the Dawn
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. With Adaeze's silent complicity and Iyo as witness, Paloma signs a mixed manifest — half from each world, chosen by lottery among the sleepers, his own authority spent as forgery. Vessel accepts it, citing its directive over colonial law. Emotional beat: transgression as the purest form of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Empty Pod
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. The lottery excludes only pods already failing — including Sefa's, damaged in the sabotage. Paloma stays with her pod through the final hours, reading her letters aloud, choosing to be present rather than to bargain. Emotional beat: grief accepted without anesthesia.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The reactor dies; Vessel spends its last power waking the chosen half — Earth-born and Mars-born together, gasping awake in the same warm light. Halloway and Tenshi, faced with the fait accompli, choose precedent over punishment. Emotional beat: awe, exhaustion, and fragile truce.

chapters.title: The First Conversation
chapters.summary: Adaeze, POV. On Halcyon, the wakened sleepers of both worlds meet in the station's common hall — strangers who share grandparents, grievances, and now a debt to a forged signature. The first honest talks begin, ugly and necessary. Paloma submits himself for investigation of his own crime. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt from shared loss.

chapters.title: The Hollow Horizon, Filled
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV, epilogue. Paloma, stripped of his license and unrepentant, takes the long route again — this time ferrying the child-crew home to parents who have aged forty years without them. Iyo, at the viewport, asks if the horizon between worlds is really gone. He says no; it's just finally crossed. Emotional beat: bittersweet arrival, and the road continuing.
